title: What If You Ran in Cinderella's Glass Slippers?
lines: Gus is wearing glass slippers strong enough to hold up two elephants, and they're about to break under him.
It's eleven at night at the neighbor's costume party, and Gus came as Cinderella.
His wife can't look. Glass shoes? He'll go right through them.
Gus stands up. Nothing. He hops. Nothing. He dances with the neighbor. Still nothing.
But wait. A dropped cup breaks on the floor. So why not a shoe with Gus on top?
You see, glass loves a squeeze. Press on it and it pushes back harder than concrete.
A glass cube smaller than a sugar cube can carry ten tons. That's two elephants on one heel.
Then the clock strikes twelve, and Gus runs.
Now every step lands with two and a half times his weight, and it lands crooked.
So the heel bends. One side gets squeezed and the other gets stretched.
And stretched glass is twenty-five times weaker.
Ever try to rip open a bag of chips? It won't tear until you find the little notch.
Glass is covered in tiny scratches too small to see. Pull on one and it runs right through.
Luckily, a squeeze holds every scratch shut.
Unluckily, Gus is in a hurry.
Snap. One heel is gone, three steps from the gate.
So Gus hops home in one glass slipper, which is exactly how the story goes.
